title: iWoz: Computer Geek to Cult Icon – How I Invented the Personal Computer, Co-Founded Apple, and Had Fun Doing It
author: Steve Wozniak with Gina Smith
target_audience: Fans of Apple and Silicon Valley history
Readers interested in personal and professional journeys
core_themes: Collaboration and partnership (especially with Steve Jobs)
Tech industry and Silicon Valley culture
primary_purpose: To share Steve Wozniak's personal story of inventing the personal computer, co-founding Apple, and highlighting the importance of curiosity, play, and ethical engineering in changing the world.

structure_format.organization: Chronological, beginning with childhood, moving through early tinkering, invention of the Apple I and II, Apple’s founding, and later reflections
features: Technical and engineering insights explained clearly
Personal reflections on success, failure, and values

key_concepts_lessons: Passion for learning and exploration can drive innovation.
Persistence and working through setbacks are essential to breakthrough inventions.
Collaboration and respectful partnerships can catalyze success.
Maintaining personal ethics—such as fairness and sharing credit—is critical in business.
Play and enjoyment in work fuel creativity.
Technological impact comes from making tools accessible to ordinary people.
notable_features: Technical stories made accessible to non-experts
Focus on personal motivation and values over corporate drama
Cartoon illustrations and personal photos in some editions
cultural_historical_context: Written during a period of renewed interest in Apple and technology legends, the memoir provides a first-hand perspective on the formative years of the personal computer revolution and Silicon Valley’s unique culture.
reception_impact: Widely praised for its candid, humble tone and technical insights
Valued for demystifying early computing history
Appreciated by tech fans and general readers alike
Some critics note the book focuses more on Wozniak’s technical journey than Apple’s business drama
comparable_titles: Hackers: Heroes of the Computer Revolution by Steven Levy
Fire in the Valley: The Birth and Death of the Personal Computer by Paul Freiberger and Michael Swaine
